scope: Proposition 2.2 (Two complete directions) of the manuscript “Every complex K3 surface is Oka” (preprints/Every-complex-K3-surface-is-Oka-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 042 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c35e20c01dcefe76), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose there are holomorphic maps σ1 : C × ∆b −→ X, σ2 : ∆b × C −→ X which are locally biholomorphic at (0, 0) and satisfy σ1(z, 0) = σ2(z, 0) for small z. If σ2 is locally biholomorphic at (0, c), then L holds at x = σ2(0, c). The same conclusion holds for a sequence of pairs whose long coordinate domains are discs of radii tending to infinity, whose bounded-coordinate radii are bounded below, and whose maps converge near (0, 0) and, for the second map, near (0, c) to the above nondegenerate germs. Exact axis agreement is required for every pair. In this version x is the value of the limiting second germ at (0, c).
